conclusions.question: (a) What do the SRV records of the plain and .global. hosts return, and what do their targets point to?
conclusions.answer: Each host has exactly one SRV record, port 10260, priority 0, weight 0, TTL 30 s: _mongodb._tcp.ddb-samples-shared.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com -> fc-a472369cc681-000.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com; _mongodb._tcp.ddb-samples-shared.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com -> fc-a472369cc681-000.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com (the target keeps the .global. label). Targets: fc-a472369cc681-000.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com CNAME fc-a472369cc681-000.privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com A 20.42.93.93; fc-a472369cc681-000.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com CNAME fc-a472369cc681-000.global.privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com A 20.42.93.93; no AAAA. Neither host has a TXT record (no options come from DNS) and neither cluster host has an A record (NOERROR/NODATA), so both exist only as SRV names. One SRV target matches one shard / one node.

conclusions.question: (b) Does the .global. form resolve and authenticate on a single-region cluster with no replica?
conclusions.answer: Yes. With MANAGED_GLOBAL_URI PyMongo 4.20.1 resolved SRV to the .global. node name (its shared-parent-domain check passes), ping returned ok 1.0, connectionStatus showed factoryadmin@admin with role root (SCRAM-SHA-256), insert_one and find worked, and documents written through either form were visible through both. The cluster was a single Primary: replica.role 'Primary', `replica list` [], HA Disabled, shardCount 1. hello through the two forms differs only in endpointName. This is the first observation of the .global. form in this project; DECISIONS topic 3 had it as documented-only.

conclusions.question: (b, extra) Which non-SRV mongodb:// host forms work?
conclusions.answer: mongodb://ddb-samples-shared.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com:10260 and mongodb://ddb-samples-shared.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com:10260 fail after serverSelectionTimeoutMS with ServerSelectionTimeoutError '[Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known' because the cluster hosts have no A record. mongodb://fc-a472369cc681-000.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com:10260, mongodb://fc-a472369cc681-000.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com:10260 and mongodb://fc-a472369cc681-000.ro.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com:10260 (a name found only in the TLS certificate) all authenticate and read. So the cluster host must be used with mongodb+srv; a non-SRV string needs the SRV target, a node name (fc-<id>-000...) that appears in no service-issued connection string (Learn's Private Link page shows such names only as SRV targets).

conclusions.question: (c) What does az documentdb mongocluster list-connection-strings return, and does it include a global string?
conclusions.answer: Parameters (from --help): -g/--resource-group and --cluster-name (or --ids). Output: {"connectionStrings": [{"connectionString": "mongodb+srv://<user>:<password>@ddb-samples-shared.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com/?tls=true&authMechanism=SCRAM-SHA-256&retrywrites=false&maxIdleTimeMS=120000", "description": "Global read-write cluster connection string", "name": "GlobalReadWrite"}, {"connectionString": "mongodb+srv://<user>:<password>@ddb-samples-shared.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com/?tls=true&authMechanism=SCRAM-SHA-256&retrywrites=false&maxIdleTimeMS=120000", "description": "Cluster connection string", "name": "Self"}]}. Yes, it returns the global string, listed first, on a single cluster with no replica. The strings carry literal '<user>:<password>' placeholders, so there was nothing to mask. The REST action returns the same two entries at api-versions 2026-09-01 and 2026-10-15-preview (the CLI sends 2026-06-01). GET properties.connectionString is the Self (plain) string. This settles DECISIONS topic 3 open item 1 for a single cluster with NativeAuth only: names are 'GlobalReadWrite' and 'Self'. The REST reference samples (one unnamed entry described 'default connection string') do not match the live response. Whether an Entra ID entry appears when MicrosoftEntraID auth is enabled, and what a replica's list holds, were not tested because both need configuration changes.

conclusions.question: (c, implication) Is connectionStrings[0] the plain host?
conclusions.answer: No. Array position 0 is GlobalReadWrite (.global. host), while GET properties.connectionString gives the Self (plain) string. Code and agents should select an entry by name ('Self' or 'GlobalReadWrite'), not by index, and should not assume the 'default' string is in the list at position 0.

conclusions.question: (d) What do hello and buildInfo report, and how does that compare with the open-source engine?
conclusions.answer: hello: isWritablePrimary true, msg 'isdbgrid', maxBsonObjectSize 16777216, maxMessageSizeBytes 48000000, maxWriteBatchSize 25000, logicalSessionTimeoutMinutes 30, minWireVersion 0, maxWireVersion 25, endpointName '<SRV target the client used>', readOnly false, saslSupportedMechs ['SCRAM-SHA-256'], internal {documentdb_versions ['2.2-1','2.3.0','12.1-1'], kind 'azuredocumentdb'}, ok 1.0, operationTime <Timestamp>. buildInfo: {version '8.0.0', versionArray [8,0,0,0], bits 64, maxBsonObjectSize 16777216, ok 1.0}. buildInfo does NOT carry internal.documentdb_versions; only hello (and isMaster) do. Against documentdb-local 0.117: hello differs in maxWireVersion (25 vs 21), documentdb_versions (3 entries vs ['0.117-0','0.117.0']), kind ('azuredocumentdb' vs ''), and adds endpointName and operationTime; all limits and the SASL list are the same. buildInfo has the same keys with version 8.0.0 vs 7.0.0. Both answer identically through the plain and .global. forms apart from endpointName.

conclusions.question: (d) Are getCmdLineOpts and getParameter '*' allowed?
conclusions.answer: Both are allowed for the root admin user. getCmdLineOpts returns {argv: [], ok: 1.0} with no 'parsed' section. getParameter '*' returns eight parameters: failpoint.disablePipelineOptimization false, featureFlagCollModIndexUnique false, featureFlagTimeseriesMetricIndexes false, internalDocumentSourceDensifyMaxMemoryBytes 104857600, internalQueryEnableSlotBasedExecutionEngine true, internalQueryForceClassicEngine true, internalQueryMaxAllowedDensifyDocs 500000, transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds 30. Single parameters from that list can be read (transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds -> 30), but {getParameter: 1, featureCompatibilityVersion: 1} fails with {ok: 0.0, errmsg: 'No option found for get'} with no code or codeName, so tools that read the FCV get an uncoded OperationFailure. The OSS run only listed getCmdLineOpts and getParameter as cluster privileges; it never executed them.

conclusions.question: (d) Does PyMongo print a CosmosDB warning, and when?
conclusions.answer: Yes. PyMongo 4.20.1 emits UserWarning 'You appear to be connected to a CosmosDB cluster. For more information regarding feature compatibility and support please visit https://www.mongodb.com/supportability/cosmosdb' for every host ending in '.cosmos.azure.com' (pymongo/mongo_client_shared.py _detect_external_db). With default filters it is printed twice for each mongodb+srv URI, plain or .global.: once at the caller's MongoClient(...) line and once at pymongo/synchronous/mongo_client.py:1916 (self._resolve_srv()), because the SRV-resolved node names match too. A non-SRV client prints it once. Connections still work. From the code (not exercised here), it is logged at INFO instead of warned when the 'pymongo.client' logger is enabled for INFO. It cannot fire against documentdb-local at localhost.

conclusions.question: What names does the service's TLS certificate cover?
conclusions.answer: One TLSv1.3 certificate (CN ed484574ee80.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, issuer Microsoft TLS G2 RSA CA OCSP 04, notBefore Nov 25 20:27:37 2026 GMT, notAfter Mar 5 19:27:37 2027 GMT) is served for both SRV targets, and it verifies against the default CA store. Its SANs are fc-a472369cc681-000.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, ddb-samples-shared.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, ddb-samples-shared.data.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, ddb-samples-shared.data.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, fc-a472369cc681-000.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, fc-a472369cc681-000.ro.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com and ed484574ee80.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com. ddb-samples-shared.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com is not a SAN, which is harmless because it has no A record and clients connect to the SRV target. The local container uses a self-signed certificate with tlsAllowInvalidCertificates, so there is nothing to compare.

conclusions.question: Are there host forms beyond plain and .global.?
conclusions.answer: Yes, by observation, but none appears in the service-issued connection strings or in the sources DECISIONS topic 3 cites. fc-a472369cc681-000.ro.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com (a certificate SAN) CNAMEs to fc-a472369cc681-000.ro.global.privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, resolves to the same IP and accepts SCRAM connections; hello through it reports isWritablePrimary true and readOnly false on this single cluster. _mongodb._tcp.ddb-samples-shared.ro.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com exists (NOERROR, while an invented name gives NXDOMAIN) but holds no SRV, TXT, CNAME or A record. The Data API hosts ddb-samples-shared.data.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com and ddb-samples-shared.data.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com both resolve (the global one is a CNAME to the self one, then to the node), so both forms on the Data API Learn page are real names; they have no MongoDB SRV record. Inferred, not verified: '.ro.global.' is a read-only global endpoint that would point at a replica once one exists; behaviour with a replica needs a later test.

conclusions.question: Does the public DNS chain support the private-endpoint best guess in DECISIONS topic 3 open item 2?
conclusions.answer: It supports it but does not settle it. In public DNS the .global. node name has its own CNAME into the privatelink namespace (fc-a472369cc681-000.global.privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com), separate from the plain node's fc-a472369cc681-000.privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com, and the .ro.global. node has a third (fc-a472369cc681-000.ro.global.privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com); cluster names have no privatelink record (NXDOMAIN). So a private DNS zone named privatelink.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com would need records '<node>', '<node>.global' (and '<node>.ro.global') for the .global. form to resolve privately, which matches the Microsoft Q&A nslookup. Resolution through a real private endpoint was not tested (none exists, and Phase 1 forbids configuration changes).

conclusions.question: Do the service-issued connection strings agree with the retryWrites decision and the ALLOWED_HOSTS guidance?
conclusions.answer: Yes. Both service-issued strings (CLI, REST at three api-versions, GET) contain retrywrites=false and maxIdleTimeMS=120000, consistent with the 'retrywrites=false is required' decision. The SRV-resolved hosts are node names (fc-<id>-000[.global|.ro.global].mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com), not the cluster name in the URI. This is the case the Mongoose tutorial describes for ALLOWED_HOSTS: '*.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com' covers every observed node name, since the auth spec allows nested subdomains. OIDC itself was not exercised (NativeAuth only), so the ALLOWED_HOSTS part is inferred.

decisions_topic: DECISIONS.md, 'Host forms' (SME topic 3): settled items confirmed by observation; open item 1 answered for a single cluster; open item 2 supported (inferred); open item 3 not in scope (needs a replica and a promotion).
